Hon'ble Shri Arvind Kumar Verma, Judge Order on Board 18.07.2025
1.

This writ petition has been preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking following reliefs:
"10.1.

That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow this petition and quash the impugned orders dated may kindly be quash/set-aside the impugned order dated 13.06.2025 (ANNEXURE P/1), impugned order dated 13.06.2025 (ANNEXURE P/2)
and impugned order dated 15.04.2025 (ANNEXURE P/3), in the interest of justice.

10.2. That the Hon'ble court may kindly direct the respondents to allow the petitioner to continue running the mid-day meal program at Government Swami Atmanand School Balco, in the interest of justice.
10.3. Any other relief which deemed fit and proper may also be issued looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the interest of justice."

2. By the present writ petition, the petitioner is questioning the impugned order Annexure P/1 &
P-2, by which, respondent-authority has terminated the allotment of the mid-day meal order which has been issued in favour of the petitioner.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that impugned order is a non-speaking order as same has been passed only on the basis of enquiry report and without giving proper opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.

4. Learned State Counsel submits that based on the complaint made with regard to the quality of the food supplied by the petitioner is not upto the mark, the Committee has been constituted to enquire the food quality supplied by the petitioner in the Swami Atmanand English School.
The Inquiry Officer has made an enquiry and submitted the report vide Annexure P-3 before the concerned respondent-authority.

The Committee has found that there is poor quality of food supplied by the petitioner and, thereafter, respondent-authority has passed the impugned order and detached the petitioner from the work of preparation of Mid-Day-Meal in Swami Atmanand English School,
Balco, Korba, District Korba, (CG).

Vide Annexure P-3, following suggestion has been given:
" :-

-

2             
            - 
 
5.

Learned State Counsel further contended that during the enquiry petitioner was not present on the spot, therefore, opportunity of hearing could not be given to him, however,
respondent-authorities are ready to re-enquire the matter after providing proper opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material/documents available on record including the impugned order.
7. In the earlier round of litigation, vide order dated 25.03.2025 in WPC No.5424/2022, this Court has passed the following order/direction:

"Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, at this stage, prima facie, it appears that there is nothing against the petitioner and the petitioner is running the midday meal in accordance with law.
The petitioner society may continue the midday meal Programme.
However, if any complaint is made against the petitioner, the respondent authorities are at liberty to proceed in accordance with law.

7. With the aforesaid observations/directions, instant writ petition is disposed of"
8.

Considering above facts of the case, submissions of counsel for the parties, writ petition is disposed of at this stage permitting the petitioner to submit fresh representation before the concerned respondents- authorities within 15 days and in-turn concerned Authority shall conduct an enquiry regarding testing/verifying the quality of food supplied by the petitioner and also give proper opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and, thereafter, pass appropriate order on its own merit within 30 days from the date of receipt of copy of such representation.
9.
The respondent-authority concerned is directed to permit/allow the petitioner-group to continue the work of preparation of Mid-Day-Meal in the concerned School till the inquiry is completed

,
however, petitioner- group is also directed to maintain the hygiene and quality of food as per standard of the food Safety.
CC as per rules.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Arvind Kumar Verma)
 Judge J/-
